[[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] '''Insmot Bowen''' was a [[Human/Legends|human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] member of the [[Obroan Institute for Archaeology]], who specialized in the history of the [[Pre-Republic era]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|Human history begins with our tenure as particularly useful Rakatan slaves, serving the greater glory of the Infinite Empire.|Insmot Bowen|<ref name="EGTWAC" />}}
At some point prior to [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], Bowen joined the Obroan Institute for Archaeology. In 1 BBY, he met with several Imperials for a debriefing regarding Celestials and their technology. During the meeting, which was made up of Bowen, [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]], Dr. [[Bevel Lemelisk]], and [[General/Legends|General]] [[Arhul Kurumenga]] from the [[Imperial Department of Military Research/Legends|Imperial Department of Military Research]], Bowen presented a theory that strange occurrences in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], including a [[Western barrier|barrier]] to the west of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], were remnants of [[Celestial/Legends|Celestial]] technology dating back to the [[Rakatan revolt]]. Admiral Motti, a staunch non-believer in the supernatural, refused to believe him,<ref name="JLT">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/20843004826/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-1|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 1}}</ref> and frequently mocked him throughout the debriefing.<ref name="EGTWAC" />

==Behind the scenes==
Dr. Insmot Bowen was created for the original prologue of ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''. However, the character was cut because [[Erich Schoeneweiss]], the editor at [[Del Rey]], felt that the prologue would not get people involved in the book, and that a firsthand account of a battle would be more appropriate. [[Jason Fry]], one of the authors, begrudgingly complied, replacing Bowen's conversation with an account of the [[Battle of Andalia]] by [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Osvald Teshik]].<ref name="JLT" />

The character later appeared in the first part of the 12-part blog series [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], "The Celestials," on [[Star Wars Blog]]. He, alongside the entire segment, was vetted as canon within [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] by [[Leland Chee]].
